earnings_release.text: EX-99.1 2 kmi2026q38-kex991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 KINDER MORGAN REPORTS RECORD THIRD QUARTER 2026 FINANCIAL RESULTS Announces $5.4 Billion of Additions to Expansion Project Backlog Largest Natural Gas Project Backlog in Company’s History Earnings per share (EPS) and Adjusted EPS both 21% higher than 2025 HOUSTON, October 21, 2026 - Kinder Morgan, Inc.’s (NYSE: KMI) board of directors today approved a cash dividend of $0.2975 per share for the third quarter ($1.19 annualized), payable on November 16, 2026, to stockholders of record as of the close of business on November 2, 2026. This dividend is a 2% increase over the third quarter of 2025. KMI is reporting all-time record third quarter results: • Third quarter net income attributable to KMI of $764 million. This was up from $628 million in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted Net Income Attributable to KMI, which excludes Certain Items, was $792 million, 22% higher than the third quarter of 2025. • Adjusted EBITDA of $2.18 billion, up 9% versus the third quarter of 2025. • EPS of $0.34, up 21% versus the third quarter of 2025, and Adjusted EPS of $0.35, also up 21% versus the third quarter of 2025. • Largest natural gas expansion project backlog in company history, at $13.2 billion of an overall $14.4 billion project backlog. Executive Chairman Richard D. Kinder said, “Our record-setting performance is firmly grounded in our long-standing business model. We enjoy a strategically located network of assets and a portfolio of long-term, fee-based contracts with financially strong customers, providing stable and predictable cash flows. “Our natural gas business in particular is benefiting from increasing LNG exports, rising power demand, and industrial expansion and is capitalizing on significant opportunities for investment across our footprint,” said Kinder. “We expect those investments to generate attractive returns, driving future earnings and cash flows to support a growing dividend and maintain a strong balance sheet, all while helping meet growing energy demand in the United States and the world.” Chief Executive Officer Kim Dang said, “This quarter we increased our expansion project backlog to $14.4 billion, including the largest natural gas project backlog in company history at $13.2 billion. Two new major projects in the backlog include Southern Natural Gas Company’s (SNG) Southeast Connector and Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America’s (NGPL) Permian Link. Each project is designed to transport over 2.5 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) of natural gas and will be among the largest natural gas pipeline projects to be constructed in decades. The Southeast Connector Project is especially transformative in that it will deliver abundant Marcellus/Utica supply to the Southeast, one of the fastest growing demand centers in the country. “Along with the August announcement of our Western Gateway Pipeline Project, which will deliver refined products to Arizona and, for the first time via pipeline, to California, these projects will optimize energy flows in multiple regions of the U.S. We are proud to be leading that effort. “We are equally proud of the financial and operational excellence that resulted in a record third quarter. Strong financial contributions from our business segments delivered third quarter 2026 net income attributable to KMI of $764 million, 22% higher than the third quarter of 2025, while Adjusted EPS and Adjusted EBITDA were 21% and 9% higher, respectively, than the third quarter of 2025.” Dang continued, “Throughout the year we have continued to internally fund high-quality capital projects while generating stable cash flow from operations of $5 billion and free cash flow, after capital expenditures and dividends, of $230 million. Our balance sheet remains healthy, as we ended the quarter with a Net Debt-to-Adjusted EBITDA ratio of 3.5 times, at the low end of our targeted range. “As noted above, the expansion project backlog at the end of the third quarter was $14.4 billion, up $4.7 billion from the second quarter of 2026, with $5.4 billion of additions net of $700 million in projects placed in service. More than 75% of the total backlog is associated with projects supporting power generation and local distribution company demand. As our record-setting performance indicates, the strong interest from our customers in developing additional natural gas infrastructure continues to grow. “In calculating backlog Project EBITDA multiples, we exclude both the capital and EBITDA from our CO 2 enhanced oil recovery projects and our gathering and processing projects where first-full-year multiples are more favorable, but the earnings are more uneven than with our other business segments. The larger $13.7 billion portion of the backlog represents stable, primarily take-or-pay cash flows. When those projects are realized, we expect them to generate an aggregate first-full-year Project EBITDA multiple of approximately 5.7 times.” 2026 Outlook For 2026, KMI budgeted net income attributable to KMI of $3.1 billion, Adjusted EPS of $1.36, declared dividends of $1.19 per share, Adjusted EBITDA of $8.6 billion, and year-end Net Debt-to-Adjusted EBITDA of 3.8 times. KMI currently expects to be more than 6% favorable to budget on an Adjusted EBITDA basis and more than 13% favorable to budget on an Adjusted EPS basis for the year. KMI also expects to end the year with a Net Debt-to-Adjusted EBITDA ratio of 3.6 times, which is 0.2 times favorable to KMI’s budget. This press release includes Adjusted Net Income Attributable to KMI, Adjusted EPS, Adjusted Segment EBDA, Adjusted EBITDA, Net Debt, FCF, and Project EBITDA, all of which are non-GAAP financial measures. For descriptions of these non-GAAP financial measures and reconciliations to the most comparable measures prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, please see “Non-GAAP Financial Measures” and the tables accompanying KMI’s preliminary financial statements. Overview of Business Segments KMI President Dax Sanders stated, “The Natural Gas Pipelines business segment’s financial performance was up in the third quarter of 2026 relative to the third quarter of 2025, on higher contributions from the El Paso Natural Gas Pipeline (EPNG), KinderHawk gathering system, Tennessee Gas Pipeline (TGP), and our Texas Intrastate system. “Natural gas transport volumes were up 3% compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to LNG deliveries on TGP and increased demand for services on our Texas Intrastate system. “Natural gas gathering volumes were up 14% from the third quarter of 2025, primarily on our KinderHawk system.” Sanders added, “While the Products Pipelines business segment had favorable contributions compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to favorable commodity pricing, these were more than offset by legal, environmental, and other expense accruals, which are treated as Certain Items. “Total refined products volumes were down 3% compared to the third quarter of 2025, due to a higher commodity price environment over the quarter. Crude and condensate volumes were down 11% compared to the third quarter of 2025, due to lower gathered volumes in the Bakken and the conversion of our Double H pipeline to natural gas liquids service.” Sanders continued, “ Terminals business segment earnings were up compared to the third quarter of 2025 on higher liquids contributions from expansion projects placed into service, higher commodity prices, increased strength in our coal and petroleum coke handling activities, and higher rates on our Jones Act tanker fleet. “ CO 2 business segment earnings, which include the Energy Transition Ventures group, were up compared to the third quarter of 2025, due primarily to higher commodity prices and higher crude and NGL volumes. Volumes at SACROC, our largest field, were up 11% compared to the prior year period, and NGL sales volumes were up 9%.” Other News Corporate • On August 6, 2026, KMI issued $1.15 billion of 5.55% senior notes due August 2036 and $600 million of 6.15% senior notes due August 2056. The proceeds were used to repay outstanding commercial paper and maturing debt and for general corporate purposes. Natural Gas Pipelines • SNG has reached a final investment decision to proceed with the Southeast Connector Project (SEC Project) after securing sufficient long-term, take-or-pay transportation agreements with shippers. The SEC Project is designed to transport up to 2.6 Bcf/d of natural gas and includes approximately 470 miles of new pipeline and new and expanded compression infrastructure to serve growing markets in the Southeast. The project can be scaled further with additional customer commitments. The KMI share of the total project cost is expected to be $3.1 billion, though final capacity and capital expenditure levels will be determined depending on the ultimate project scope. Subject to the timely receipt of all required permits and approvals, the SEC Project is expected to be placed in service in phases beginning in the fourth quarter of 2030. • NGPL has reached a final investment decision to proceed with its Permian Link Project. The approximately $4.2 billion project (KMI-share approximately $1.6 billion) is designed to provide approximately 2.8 Bcf/d of natural gas transportation capacity through the construction of approximately 434 miles of new pipeline and related compression, metering, and interconnect facilities. The project will serve new power generation for an A-rated hyperscaler and is supported by long-term, take-or-pay transportation agreements. Subject to the timely receipt of all required permits and approvals, the Permian Link Project is expected to be placed in service in the third quarter of 2030. • KMI has sanctioned a $95 million second phase and $55 million third phase of its Creekside Lateral Project following the execution of additional long-term, take-or-pay agreements with data center and industrial customers. Upon completion of all phases, this approximately $235 million intrastate project is expected to provide more than 750 million cubic feet per day of contracted natural gas transportation to serve growing demand in Central Texas. The project has capacity to transport approximately 1.3 Bcf/d, with future expansion potential above 2 Bcf/d. Subject to the timely receipt of all required permits and approvals, KMI expects to place the projects in service in phases, first in the fourth quarter of 2026 and then in the fourth quarter of 2027. • SNG and TGP have reached a final investment decision to proceed with the Bear Creek Storage Expansion Project. The approximately $160 million project (KMI-share approximately $120 million) includes a base natural gas conversion and facility expansion that will support the leasing of approximately 10 Bcf of storage capacity to TGP for which TGP has secured long-term binding agreements. Subject to the timely receipt of all required permits and approvals, the project is expected to be placed in service in April 2029. • The Plantation North Expansion Project on KMI’s KinderHawk gathering system is nearing completion. The more than $500 million project, backed by life-of-lease acreage dedications, supports projected production growth from the Haynesville Basin and increasing LNG demand along the Gulf Coast. The project is expected to be completed by year-end 2026. Products Pipelines • On August 11, 2026, KMI, Phillips 66, and HF Sinclair announced a final joint venture agreement and reached a final investment decision to move forward with the proposed Western Gateway Pipeline. With a design capacity of approximately 230,000 barrels per day, the approximately 1,300-mile refined products pipeline system would create a new fuel supply path from the Midwest and Gulf Coast regions to markets in Arizona and California, with connectivity to Las Vegas, Nevada, via KMI’s CALNEV Pipeline. reference.summary: Kinder Morgan, Inc. operates as an energy infrastructure company primarily in North America. It operates through Natural Gas Pipelines, Products Pipelines, Terminals, and CO2 segments. The Natural Gas Pipelines segment owns and operates interstate and intrastate natural gas pipeline, and storage systems; natural gas gathering systems and natural gas processing and treating facilities; natural gas liquids fractionation facilities and transportation systems; and liquefied natural gas gasification, liquefaction, and storage facilities. The Products Pipelines segment owns and operates refined petroleum products, and crude oil and condensate pipelines; and associated product terminals and petroleum pipeline transmix facilities.
